cond_0001.intro:
The way we are securing computer systems is not working, come help us change the paradigm as we apply formal techniques to system security. Modern computing systems are complex. As scientists we deal with complexity by utilizing abstraction. Thus layered system architectures are the foundation of all modern computing systems. Yet these system layers can interact in ways that people who use them (and even the people who designed and built them) do not understand. This paves the way for attackers to exploit systems.
[Company name masked]'s Secure and Resilient Systems group is working to change this paradigm. We are developing new theories, techniques, and tooling to support scalable system security analysis using formal methods. If you have a background with existing formal methods tools like Coq, TLA+, EasyCrypt, and SMT solvers, F*, we would love to talk.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Use formal methods to model complex systems
Provide feedback to our tool development team on ways to make the tools we develop better
Research new methods to make application of formal methods to systems we are analyzing better
Build new formal methods tools
Participate in relevant internal and customer meetings
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Cybersecurity and 8 years of relevant experience, 6 years and a Masters, or 3 years and a PhD
Prior experience with formal methods tools
A deep technical understanding of cybersecurity problems and solutions
Experience with modern software development tools and practices
Self-starter and ability to manage time and technical tasks independently without direct supervision
Preferred Requirements
MS or PhD degree in related technical field
Experience with cryptography and formal methods applied to cryptography
Experience writing peer-reviewed technical papers
Experience giving presentations to technical peers and leaders

As scientists we deal with complexity by utilizing abstraction. Thus layered system architectures are the foundation of all modern computing systems. [Company name masked]'s Secure and Resilient Systems group is working to change this paradigm. cond_0099.intro:
The way we are securing computer systems is not working, and we are working to change that paradigm by applying formal techniques to system security. Modern computing systems are complex. As scientists we deal with complexity by utilizing abstraction. Thus layered system architectures are the foundation of all modern computing systems. Yet these system layers can interact in ways that people who use them (and even the people who designed and built them) do not understand. This paves the way for attackers to exploit systems.
[Company name masked]'s Secure and Resilient Systems group is working to change this paradigm together. We are developing new theories, techniques, and tooling to support scalable system security analysis using formal methods. If you have a background with existing formal methods tools like Coq, TLA+, EasyCrypt, and SMT solvers, F*, we would love to talk.

cond_0152.intro:
The way we are securing computer systems is not working, come help us change the paradigm as we apply formal techniques to system security. Modern computing systems are complex. As scientists we deal with complexity by utilizing abstraction. Thus layered system architectures are the foundation of all modern computing systems. Yet these system layers can interact in ways that people who use them (and even the people who designed and built them) do not understand. This paves the way for attackers to exploit systems.
[Company name masked]'s Secure and Resilient Systems group is working to change this paradigm. We are developing new theories, techniques, and tooling to support scalable system security analysis using formal methods. If you have a background with existing formal methods tools like Coq, TLA+, EasyCrypt, and SMT solvers, F*, we would love to talk.
All [Company name masked] opportunities require U.S. Citizenship.
cond_0152.responsibilities:
Own the application of formal methods to model complex systems
Deliver direct feedback to our tool development team on ways to make the tools we develop better
Lead research into new methods to improve the application of formal methods to systems we are analyzing
Build new formal methods tools
Drive participation in relevant internal and customer meetings

The way we are securing computer systems is not working, come help us change the paradigm as we apply formal techniques to system security. Modern computing systems are complex. As scientists we deal with complexity by utilizing abstraction. Thus layered system architectures are the foundation of all modern computing systems. Yet these system layers can interact in ways that people who use them (and even the people who designed and built them) do not understand. This paves the way for attackers to exploit systems.
[Company name masked]'s Secure and Resilient Systems group is working to change this paradigm. We are developing new theories, techniques, and tooling to support scalable system security analysis using formal methods. If you have a background with existing formal methods tools like Coq, TLA+, EasyCrypt, and SMT solvers, F*, we would love to talk. Most people become stronger in this kind of formal methods work over time as they build experience and learn from applying these techniques to real systems.

As scientists we deal with complexity by utilizing abstraction. Thus layered system architectures are the foundation of all modern computing systems. Yet these system layers can interact in ways that people who use them (and even the people who designed and built them) do not understand. This paves the way for attackers to exploit systems.
[Company name masked]'s Secure and Resilient Systems group is working to change this paradigm together. We are developing new theories, techniques, and tooling to support scalable system security analysis using formal methods. If you have a background with existing formal methods tools like Coq, TLA+, EasyCrypt, and SMT solvers, F*, we would love to talk.
All [Company name masked] opportunities require U.S. Citizenship.
cond_0279.responsibilities:
Work with the team to model complex systems using formal methods
Share feedback with our tool development team on ways to improve the tools we develop
Collaborate on research into new methods to make application of formal methods to systems we are analyzing better
Contribute to building new formal methods tools alongside colleagues
Participate in relevant internal and customer meetings
cond_0279.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Cybersecurity and 8 years of relevant experience, 6 years and a Masters, or 3 years and a PhD
Prior experience with formal methods tools
A deep technical understanding of cybersecurity problems and solutions
Experience with modern software development tools and practices
Ability to manage time and technical tasks with limited direct supervision
Preferred Requirements
MS or PhD degree in a related technical field
Experience with cryptography and formal methods applied to cryptography
Experience writing peer-reviewed technical papers
Experience giving presentations to technical peers and leaders

cond_0332.intro:
The way we are securing computer systems is not working, come help us change the paradigm as we apply formal techniques to system security. Modern computing systems are complex. As scientists we deal with complexity by utilizing abstraction. Thus layered system architectures are the foundation of all modern computing systems. Yet these system layers can interact in ways that people who use them (and even the people who designed and built them) do not understand. This paves the way for attackers to exploit systems.
[Company name masked]'s Secure and Resilient Systems group is working to change this paradigm. We are developing new theories, techniques, and tooling to support scalable system security analysis using formal methods. If you have a background with existing formal methods tools like Coq, TLA+, EasyCrypt, and SMT solvers, F*, we would love to talk.
All [Company name masked] opportunities require U.S. Citizenship.
cond_0332.responsibilities:
Own the application of formal methods to model complex systems
Deliver direct feedback to our tool development team on ways to make the tools we develop better
Lead research into new methods to improve the application of formal methods to systems we are analyzing
Build new formal methods tools
Drive participation in relevant internal and customer meetings

cond_0345.intro:
We are looking for a Research Scientist in Formal Methods to join our team.
All opportunities require U.S. Citizenship.
The way we are securing computer systems is not working, come help us change the paradigm as we apply formal techniques to system security. Modern computing systems are complex. As scientists we deal with complexity by utilizing abstraction. Thus layered system architectures are the foundation of all modern computing systems. Yet these system layers can interact in ways that people who use them (and even the people who designed and built them) do not understand. This paves the way for attackers to exploit systems.
[Company name masked]'s Secure and Resilient Systems group is working to change this paradigm. We are developing new theories, techniques, and tooling to support scalable system security analysis using formal methods. If you have a background with existing formal methods tools like Coq, TLA+, EasyCrypt, and SMT solvers, F*, we would love to talk.

Modern computing systems are complex. As scientists we deal with complexity by utilizing abstraction. Thus layered system architectures are the foundation of all modern computing systems. Yet these system layers can interact in ways that people who use them (and even the people who designed and built them) do not understand. This paves the way for attackers to exploit systems.
[Company name masked]'s Secure and Resilient Systems group is developing new theories, techniques, and tooling to support scalable system security analysis using formal methods. If you have a background with existing formal methods tools like Coq, TLA+, EasyCrypt, SMT solvers, or F*, we would like to hear from you.
All [Company name masked] opportunities require U.S. Citizenship.
cond_0439.responsibilities:
Use formal methods to model complex systems
Provide feedback to the tool development team on ways to improve the tools being developed
Research new methods to improve the application of formal methods to systems under analysis
Build new formal methods tools
Attend relevant internal and customer meetings as required
cond_0439.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Cybersecurity and 8 years of relevant experience, 6 years and a Master's, or 3 years and a PhD
Prior experience with formal methods tools
A deep technical understanding of cybersecurity problems and solutions
Experience with modern software development tools and practices
Ability to manage time and technical tasks independently without direct supervision
Preferred Requirements
MS or PhD degree in a related technical field
Experience with cryptography and formal methods applied to cryptography
Experience writing peer-reviewed technical papers
Experience presenting findings to technical peers and leaders

cond_0530.intro:
The way we are securing computer systems is not working, come help us change the paradigm as we apply formal techniques to system security. Modern computing systems are complex. As scientists we deal with complexity by utilizing abstraction. Thus layered system architectures are the foundation of all modern computing systems. Yet these system layers can interact in ways that people who use them (and even the people who designed and built them) do not understand. This paves the way for attackers to exploit systems.
[Company name masked]'s Secure and Resilient Systems group is working to change this paradigm. We are developing new theories, techniques, and tooling to support scalable system security analysis using formal methods. If you have a background with existing formal methods tools like Coq, TLA+, EasyCrypt, and SMT solvers, F*, we would love to talk.
All [Company name masked] opportunities require U.S. Citizenship.

Own the application of formal methods to model complex systems
Deliver direct feedback to our tool development team on ways to make the tools we develop better

Drive participation in relevant internal and customer meetings

All [Company name masked] opportunities require U.S. Citizenship.
The way we are securing computer systems is not working, come help us change the paradigm as we apply formal techniques to system security. Modern computing systems are complex. As scientists we deal with complexity by utilizing abstraction. Thus layered system architectures are the foundation of all modern computing systems. Yet these system layers can interact in ways that people who use them (and even the people who designed and built them) do not understand. This paves the way for attackers to exploit systems.
[Company name masked]'s Secure and Resilient Systems group is working to change this paradigm. We are developing new theories, techniques, and tooling to support scalable system security analysis using formal methods. If you have a background with existing formal methods tools like Coq, TLA+, EasyCrypt, and SMT solvers, F*, we would love to talk.
cond_0628.responsibilities:
Use formal methods to model complex systems
Provide written feedback to our tool development team on specific ways to improve the tools we develop
Research new methods to improve the application of formal methods to systems under analysis
Build new formal methods tools
Attend relevant internal and customer meetings as required

Self-starter and ability to manage time and technical tasks independently without direct supervision
